subtitle: Cross-check of 23/Oct/2026, 19th day of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): Polymarket at the confirmed reading of 23/Oct, 19:10 BRT, the forty-three national polls conducted after the vote, including the seven released since the previous update (Datafolha, Vox Brasil, Ipespe/Abrapel, Real Time Big Data, Veritá, DataTrends and Alfa Inteligência), the official [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally and the press flow of 22 and 23/Oct.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 23.50% (cumulative volume USD 29.08M) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 23/Oct, 19:10 BRT, rises 1.00pp against the confirmed reading of 22/Oct at 17:56 BRT, published in the previous update. BALLOT: 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLLS: ahead in Vox Brasil of 23/Oct, 45.4% to 44.3%; a tie at 50% of the valid votes in Datafolha of 22/Oct, with 46% to 47% in total votes; behind in the other five released since the previous update.
fortes: He leads the three Vox Brasil polls conducted after the vote: 45.4% to 44.3% on 23/Oct, 46.4% to 44.6% on 18/Oct and 44.2% to 42.7% on 09/Oct; in the one of 23/Oct he has 50.6% of the valid votes.
In Datafolha of 22/Oct he ties at 50% of the valid votes with Flávio Bolsonaro, who in the 15/Oct wave had 51% to 49%; in Ipespe/Abrapel, his rejection is 47%, against 48% for Flávio Bolsonaro.
🏆 Counting the closed contracts, his contract is still the one with the highest cumulative volume in the presidential book, USD 29.08M.
fracos: He stands at 23.50% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 23/Oct, 19:10 BRT, and Flávio Bolsonaro's gap over him is 53.00pp.

He trails in thirty-nine of the forty-three national polls conducted after the vote, among them Ipespe/Abrapel, with 47% to 48%, Real Time Big Data, with 45% to 49%, and Veritá, with 47.5% to 50.2%, all of 23/Oct.
He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) 1.87 points behind Flávio Bolsonaro, with 45.16% of the valid votes against 47.03%.
In Real Time Big Data of 23/Oct, 36% would never vote for him, against 33% who would never vote for Flávio Bolsonaro; in Ipespe/Abrapel, the government is disapproved by 47% and approved by 45%.
candidates.analise: Lula stands at 23.50% in the winner contract (cumulative volume USD 29.08M), confirmed reading of 23/Oct, 19:10 BRT, and rises 1.00pp against the confirmed reading of 22/Oct at 17:56 BRT, published in the previous update. 🗳️ He had 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). 📊 Seven new national polls came out since the previous update. Datafolha, released on the night of 22/Oct, with 2,154 interviews from 20 to 22/Oct, gives 47% to Flávio Bolsonaro and 46% to Lula in total votes and a tie at 50% in valid votes (G1 and CartaCapital). On 23/Oct, Vox Brasil, with 2,100 in-person interviews from 20 to 22/Oct, gives 45.4% to Lula and 44.3% to Flávio Bolsonaro in total votes and 50.6% to 49.4% in valid votes (CNN Brasil and Exame). Ipespe/Abrapel, with 1,500 telephone interviews from 20 to 22/Oct, gives 48% to Flávio Bolsonaro and 47% to Lula in total votes and 50.5% to 49.5% in valid votes (Folha de S.Paulo and Exame). Real Time Big Data, with 2,000 telephone interviews from 19 to 22/Oct, gives 49% to 45% in total votes and 52% to 48% in valid votes (Congresso em Foco and CNN Brasil). Veritá, with 15,554 interviews from 18 to 22/Oct, gives 50.2% to 47.5% in total votes and 51.3% to 48.7% in valid votes (R7). DataTrends gives 50% to 46% in total votes and 51.9% to 48.1% in valid votes (Rádio Corredor). Alfa Inteligência, with 2,700 in-person interviews from 18 to 22/Oct, released only valid votes, 52% to 48% (CNN Brasil and Exame). Against each pollster's previous wave, in total votes, Datafolha goes from 47% to 45% to 47% to 46%, Ipespe/Abrapel from 48% to 46% to 48% to 47%, Real Time Big Data from 48% to 45% to 49% to 45% and Veritá from 49.7% to 48.2% to 50.2% to 47.5%; in Vox Brasil, Lula goes from 46.4% to 44.6% to 45.4% to 44.3%. In valid votes, Datafolha goes from 51% to 49% for Flávio Bolsonaro to a tie at 50%. In Vox Brasil of 23/Oct he has 45.4% against 44.3%. On 22/Oct, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro signed at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a document authorizing the lifting of their bank, tax and phone secrecy, and the release depends on Justice André Mendonça (Folha de S.Paulo, Valor and Congresso em Foco). On 23/Oct, the two campaigns delivered the authorizations to the TSE, but the data were not disclosed (UOL and O Globo), and Lula's campaign accuses Flávio Bolsonaro's of not lifting the secrecy after the agreement (Gazeta do Povo). After the promulgation, Lula said the 6x1 work schedule will return if Flávio Bolsonaro wins the election (O Globo and Valor), and on 13/Oct he announced Prospera MEI, with forgiveness of individual microentrepreneurs' debts estimated at R$ 12.6 billion (Poder360 and Estadão). ⚖️ On 20/Oct, the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) asked the Supreme Court for more time in the inquiries into alleged influence peddling by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, the president's son, and Justice Edson Fachin is to decide (Estadão and G1). ⚖️ On 23/Oct, a TSE justice granted a request by Lula's campaign and barred the court's president, Kassio Nunes Marques, from suspending the Exército do Lula channel without the plenary's approval (Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo); the day before, Nunes Marques had given Meta 24 hours to submit a report on the channel (Folha de S.Paulo and Valor). In an action by Lula's campaign, the TSE ordered Meta and X to explain the distribution of political content (CartaCapital and O Globo). ⛔ The panel does not attribute the price to the polls or to the campaign agenda: it measures the sides with each one's timestamp.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 76.50% (cumulative volume USD 25.74M) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 23/Oct, 19:10 BRT, falls 1.20pp against the confirmed reading of 22/Oct at 17:56 BRT, published in the previous update. BALLOT: 47.03% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLLS: ahead in thirty-nine of the forty-three post-vote national polls, among them Veritá of 23/Oct, 50.2% to 47.5%; a tie at 50% of the valid votes in Datafolha of 22/Oct; 44.3% to 45.4% in Vox Brasil of 23/Oct.
fortes: He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) ahead, with 47.03% of the valid votes against Lula's 45.16%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally.
He stands at 76.50% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 23/Oct, 19:10 BRT, 53.00pp ahead of Lula.

He leads thirty-nine of the forty-three national polls conducted after the vote, among them six of the seven released since the previous update, with 50.2% to 47.5% in Veritá, 49% to 45% in Real Time Big Data, 50% to 46% in DataTrends, 48% to 47% in Ipespe/Abrapel and 47% to 46% in Datafolha, in total votes, and 52% to 48% in valid votes in Alfa Inteligência.
He has the declared support of Podemos, Augusto Cury, Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer.
Among Ronaldo Caiado's voters, he has 56% against 15% in Ipespe, 54.9% against 26.9% in AtlasIntel and 57% against 19% in PoderData/Aya.
fracos: He trails in the three Vox Brasil polls conducted after the vote, with 44.3% against 45.4% on 23/Oct, 44.6% against 46.4% on 18/Oct and 42.7% against 44.2% on 09/Oct; in Datafolha of 22/Oct, the 51% to 49% lead in valid votes from the 15/Oct wave becomes a tie at 50%.

⚖️ On 18/Oct, Estadão reported, and Folha de S.Paulo and G1 confirmed, that the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) (PF) took to the Supreme Court an investigation into suspected money laundering involving the lawyer Willer Tomaz, his companies and Flávio Bolsonaro, with Alexandre de Moraes drawn as rapporteur; the case moved up from the Federal Court in Rio Grande do Sul on 08/Oct because of the senator's privileged forum (G1 and Gazeta do Povo). Flávio Bolsonaro and Willer Tomaz say they are friends and deny having business together (G1 and Gazeta do Povo). On 20/Oct, a technical note from the Finance Ministry named Willer Tomaz as the country's largest sports-betting gambler in 2025, with R$ 5 billion wagered (Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo).

⚖️ The government leader in Congress, Randolfe Rodrigues, is collecting signatures for a complaint to the Senate Ethics Council that seeks the loss of Flávio Bolsonaro's mandate for breach of decorum, citing his relationship with Daniel Vorcaro; the document has yet to be filed (Folha de S.Paulo and Valor).

🏦 According to O Globo, the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) is investigating, in the inquiry into Daniel Vorcaro and Master's relationship with BRB, the bank's R$ 3.1 million financing to Flávio Bolsonaro for the purchase of a R$ 6 million mansion in Brasília; he says the transaction was legal, and the report comes from a single media group and is included here with attribution.

📰 Messages extracted from Daniel Vorcaro's phone and published by Estadão on 24/Sep show four attempts by him to contact the banker between 13 and 16 November 2025, in the days before Vorcaro's arrest, on 17 November 2025. Gazeta do Povo confirmed the authenticity of the exchanges with its own sources close to the investigation.

In a qualitative assessment carried out during the debate with 30 groups of voters, [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) gave Flávio Bolsonaro 82 points and Lula 79, on a scale of 0 to 100 (O Globo and O Antagonista). Globo's debate, the last before the vote, is scheduled for the night of 23/Oct, in four blocks and with limits on the candidates' movement in the studio (Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão and CartaCapital). 🤝 Flávio Bolsonaro has the declared support of Podemos, Augusto Cury, Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, Michel Temer and the MDB, which on 13/Oct formalized the support of 17 state branches (Gazeta do Povo and Folha de S.Paulo); 10 MDB branches, from the North and Northeast, declared support for Lula (Estadão, Valor and CartaCapital). candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): third place, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 08/Oct (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).
fortes: He finished third, with 2.89% of the valid votes, ahead of Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado.
The [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno)'s third-place book was resolved in his favour.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid more for Renan Santos, 47.50%, and for Ronaldo Caiado, 30.00%, than for him, 23.70%.
candidates.analise: Augusto Cury finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in third, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. The first round's third-place book, which on the eve paid 23.70% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, was resolved in his favour. 🤝 On 08/Oct he declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): fourth place, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): he backs neither of the two.
fortes: He finished fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes, ahead of Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18%.
His contract in the winner book closed with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, and third place went to Augusto Cury.
candidates.analise: Renan Santos finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book, behind Lula's. On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, and it was resolved in favour of Augusto Cury. 🤝 On the night of 04/Oct he said he backs neither of the two in the second round and freed Missão's activists to choose (Gazeta do Povo and Agência Brasil).

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema, with 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad did not run for President. PRICE: the three winner contracts were closed and resolved at zero.
candidates.subtitle: The three names outside the leading pack, with the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally (100% of polling sections) and the closing of the winner contracts after the first round.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 2.18% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.82M cumulative.
caiado.fortes: He declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct, with governor Daniel Vilela (O Globo and VEJA).
caiado.fracos: He finished fifth, behind Renan Santos, and the PSD decided on neutrality in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
haddad.fortes: The top of his series in the winner contract was 7.60%, on 26/May, measured in the database backup.
haddad.fracos: He was not measured by any national poll in a presidential scenario or in a second-round pairing.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 0.27% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
zema.fortes: ⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of his voters would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), the largest transfer among the names measured (O Globo).
zema.fracos: He had 0.27% of the valid votes. He declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on 05/Oct, and Novo declared support for him on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).

candidates.analise: 🗳️ Ronaldo Caiado finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fifth, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema had 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad ran for governor of São Paulo, not for President. The three contracts in the winner book were closed by Polymarket and resolved at zero. 🤝 Romeu Zema declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on the night of 05/Oct (G1 and Folha de S.Paulo), and Novo, his party, declared support on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital). Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), even with the PSD neutral in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).
fortes: Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), and Romeu Zema declared his vote for him on 05/Oct, followed by Novo on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).
⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of Romeu Zema's voters and 42% of Ronaldo Caiado's would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (O Globo).
fracos: The two are out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and the winner contracts of all three names were resolved at zero.
Fernando Haddad did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno).

Of the forty-three national polls conducted after the vote, thirty-nine put Flávio Bolsonaro ahead, thirty-five of them by 0.6 to 9 points in total votes and four by 2.2 to 4 points in valid votes; the three Vox Brasil polls, of 09/Oct, 18/Oct and 23/Oct, put Lula ahead in total votes, by 1.5, 1.8 and 1.1 points, and PoderData/Aya of 16/Oct measured a tie in valid votes. On rejection, 36% would never vote for Lula and 33% would never vote for Flávio Bolsonaro in Real Time Big Data, and 48% reject Flávio Bolsonaro and 47% reject Lula in Ipespe/Abrapel, which measures the Lula government as disapproved by 47% and approved by 45%. 🎙️ The first debate of the second round was on Band, on the night of 18/Oct: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations over [Banco Master](/en/glossary#banco-master) and the [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) frauds, and Lula proposed that both open their families' bank and phone records (O Globo, CNN Brasil and Folha de S.Paulo). In a qualitative assessment carried out during the debate with 30 groups of voters, [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) gave Flávio Bolsonaro 82 points and Lula 79, on a scale of 0 to 100 (O Globo and O Antagonista). Globo's debate, the last before the vote, is scheduled for the night of 23/Oct, in four blocks and with limits on the candidates' movement in the studio (Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão and CartaCapital). On 22/Oct, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro signed at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a document authorizing the lifting of their bank, tax and phone secrecy, and the release depends on Justice André Mendonça (Folha de S.Paulo, Valor and Congresso em Foco). On 23/Oct, the two campaigns delivered the authorizations to the TSE, but the data were not disclosed (UOL and O Globo), and Lula's campaign accuses Flávio Bolsonaro's of not lifting the secrecy after the agreement (Gazeta do Povo). ⚖️ On 22/Oct, Justice Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, the TSE's inspector general, denied in an injunction ruling the request by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign to suspend government messages sent via WhatsApp and Gov.br, among them notices about Bolsa Família, Farmácia Popular and the INSS proof-of-life check, considering them of apparently informative content, and gave the parties five days to respond (CartaCapital, G1 and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ On 18/Oct, Estadão reported, and Folha de S.Paulo and G1 confirmed, that the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) (PF) took to the Supreme Court an investigation into suspected money laundering involving the lawyer Willer Tomaz, his companies and Flávio Bolsonaro, with Alexandre de Moraes drawn as rapporteur; the case moved up from the Federal Court in Rio Grande do Sul on 08/Oct because of the senator's privileged forum (G1 and Gazeta do Povo). Flávio Bolsonaro and Willer Tomaz say they are friends and deny having business together (G1 and Gazeta do Povo). On 20/Oct, a technical note from the Finance Ministry named Willer Tomaz as the country's largest sports-betting gambler in 2025, with R$ 5 billion wagered (Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo). ⚖️ The government leader in Congress, Randolfe Rodrigues, is collecting signatures for a complaint to the Senate Ethics Council that seeks the loss of Flávio Bolsonaro's mandate for breach of decorum, citing his relationship with Daniel Vorcaro; the document has yet to be filed (Folha de S.Paulo and Valor). ⚖️ On 20/Oct, the Federal Police asked the Supreme Court for more time in the inquiries into alleged influence peddling by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, the president's son, and Justice Edson Fachin is to decide (Estadão and G1). ⚖️ On 23/Oct, a TSE justice granted a request by Lula's campaign and barred the court's president, Kassio Nunes Marques, from suspending the Exército do Lula channel without the plenary's approval (Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo); the day before, Nunes Marques had given Meta 24 hours to submit a report on the channel (Folha de S.Paulo and Valor). In an action by Lula's campaign, the TSE ordered Meta and X to explain the distribution of political content (CartaCapital and O Globo). 🤝 Flávio Bolsonaro has the declared support of Podemos, Augusto Cury, Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, Michel Temer and the MDB, which on 13/Oct formalized the support of 17 state branches (Gazeta do Povo and Folha de S.Paulo); 10 MDB branches, from the North and Northeast, declared support for Lula (Estadão, Valor and CartaCapital). PSDB stayed neutral. Lula has the support of UP, PSTU and PCB (CNN Brasil and G1). On 16/Oct, former Fortaleza mayor Roberto Cláudio declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro (G1). Renan Santos said on 15/Oct that he does not back Lula and will not vote (O Globo and Estadão). 📜 On 16/Oct Congress promulgated the constitutional amendment (PEC) ending the 6x1 work schedule, which cuts the maximum working week from 44 to 40 hours (Gazeta do Povo, G1 and Valor), and Flávio Bolsonaro had said on 13/Oct that he would vote in favour (UOL and CNN Brasil). In BTG/Nexus of 19/Oct, 66.2% support ending the 6x1 schedule (UOL and Diário do Grande ABC). 📊 The last national polls registered with the TSE before the vote have their release scheduled for 24/Oct (Veritá, AtlasIntel, Palver, Datafolha, Phoenix, Quaest, Colectta, MDA, Nexus, 100 Cidades, Datavero and Simplex). ⛔ The panel does not attribute price moves to the polls, the debate, the inquiries or the day's acts: it measures the sides with each one's timestamps.
